title: Welcome to Kamigotchi World
introDialogue:
MENU: “Hi there, Player! Welcome to Kamigotchi World!”
MENU: “You can call me Menu. I’ll be your guide!”
MENU: “I’ll also track your items, quests, and companions while you explore.”
MENU: “You can navigate by clicking on the map to pilot your Operator.”
MENU: “Start by exploring my options and clicking around the screen.”
MENU: “When you’ve seen the basics, we can move on.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “See - that wasn’t too tricky, was it?”
MENU: “Good job!”

title: Beginning Your Journey
introDialogue:
MENU: “Feel like you’re getting the hang of my interface?”
MENU: “Excellent! Now that you’re oriented, let's start exploring your surroundings. You can move around the world using my map screen. Do you remember where it is? Go ahead and open it now.”
MENU: “There are two ways to move around in the world. You can move to an adjacent tile by clicking the red highlight on the map, or you can right click on any tile to show the harvest screen for that tile as well as fast traveling to it.”
MENU: “Movement costs five stamina, which comes out of the stamina pool shown in the bottom left corner of my interface.” 
MENU: “You have one hundred stamina to start with and you recover one point of stamina every minute, so you’ll have to plan out your moves a bit so that you don’t tire yourself out too much.”
MENU: “But go ahead and explore around for now. When you’re ready to continue, head south and you’ll see a big Torii on the edge of town.
MENU: “Once you get there, I’ll give you a Spell Card.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Here you go!”
MENU: “Spell Cards can have different effects. This one restores Stamina. If you get too tired to move, you can use it to restore yourself.”
MENU: “You can also recover Stamina by eating the right foods, or by resting and letting it recover slowly.”
MENU: “Even if you’re totally exhausted you’ll bounce back eventually, but it might take a bit of time without any items, so be careful not to run out at an inopportune moment.
MENU: “Now, let’s head into town and find you a kami.”

rewards.itemName: Neith's River of Life Spell Card

title: Your First Kami
introDialogue:
MENU: “Uh oh.”
MENU: “Something very peculiar seems to be going on with my sensors.”
MENU: “Where did that junkyard come from? Where is the town?”
MENU: “This is terrible. My databases are super messed up and the main questline is totally broken. Where is everything?”
MENU: “At least Zevana is still here. I’m gonna try and figure out what’s going on. While I’m doing that, you should talk to Zevana, she’ll set you up with your first kami.”
MENU: “I know she looks intimidating, but she’s really friendly once you get to know her!”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Good job operator! You’ve acquired your first kami!”
MENU: “Isn’t it just adorable? These cute little spirits are very useful, they’ll be your primary tool for interacting with the kamigotchi world.”
MENU: “Well, besides me, I’m also pretty primary I suppose.”
MENU: “But there’s lots of things that kami can do which I can’t.”
MENU: “Continue your journey and I’ll tell you more.”

title: What Kami Do: Harvesting
introDialogue:
MENU: “Alright, time to teach you how to use your kami. My world data might be messed up but these basic mechanics shouldn’t be too different, I hope.”
MENU: “So, if you open your party screen, you’ll be able to see your kami is currently resting while you’re holding it. Kamigotchi will rest and stay healthy when being held. Being close to an Operator seems to comfort and restore them.”
MENU: “When you send a Kami out into a room using the Start Harvest button, they’ll begin drawing the spiritual energy of the local environment into themselves.”
MENU: “We call this process Harvesting. A harvesting kami isn’t working up a sweat, kami are spirits, not animals.
MENU: “That said, harvesting does still have consequences for your kami.”
MENU: “The process of harvesting energy from a node has a slightly caustic effect on the energy of your kami’s corporeal form.”
MENU: “As a kami harvests, its HP will slowly decrease. Over time, your kami’s harvest rate will ramp up, and the rate of HP loss will ramp up with it.”
MENU: “This is very scary for a kami since it puts them at risk of being liquidated and having their corporeal form dissolved, but it’s also when a kami is at their most productive.”
MENU: “The energy a kami harvests is called $MUSU. I’ll explain more about it later.”
MENU: “You can wander around while your Kami harvest, but don’t forget where you left them! Tired Kami are vulnerable to predators.”
MENU: “Deploy your kami and do a little harvesting to get a feel for how it works.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Great! Everything seems to be working as expected.
MENU: “You might have noticed that when your kami started harvesting, you couldn’t give them orders for a little while. That’s called Cooldown.”
MENU: “Kami tend to get a little hyperfixated on whatever they’re doing, so when you send one out into a room, it’ll be very distracted and won’t listen to your instructions at first.”
MENU: “If you deploy a kami, withdraw a kami, or collect a kami’s harvest, you’ll generate a cooldown. This can be dangerous, since a kami in cooldown can’t be withdrawn to avoid predators.”
MENU: “Fortunately for you, the map tiles in this area have a level cap of 15, which should help keep your kami a bit safer from predators.”
MENU: “You’ve been a good student so far. As a reward, here’s another Spell Card!”
MENU: “You can use this one to help your Kamigotchi level up.”
MENU: “If you click your kami’s portrait in the party or harvest screen, the kami info screen will open.”
MENU: “From there you can level your kami up, and apply the skillpoint you get for that level in one of the four skill trees.”
MENU: “The kami info screen has lots of other useful information too, so be sure to look around it thoroughly.”

title: What Kami Do: Scavenging
introDialogue:
MENU: “$MUSU isn’t the only thing the Kamigotchi will collect.”
MENU: “Over time, the Harvesting action generates a force that draws objects and items to the Kami.”
MENU: “It’s like a kind of magnetism that only affects certain things.”
MENU: “Which things? Well that depends on your Kami’s location. You can see what items a kami might find in a room by checking the room details on my harvesting screen.”
MENU: “We call this action “Scavenging”.”
MENU: “Try it out and see what kind of present the Kami brings you!”
MENU: “Once you’ve collected it, I can cross reference it with my database to see if the drop tables I’ve been giving you are accurate.”
MENU: “I’ll be pretty embarrassed if they’re wrong too, but there’s only one way to find out.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Ooh cool find! And you’ll be happy to know that my loot databases appear accurate, so you can trust that what I display as scavenge on my harvest screen is the real scavenge for that room.”
MENU: “That still leaves a lot of questions, but one thing at a time.”
MENU: “If you want to know more about an item, just open your inventory and take a closer look.”

title: What Kami Do: Liquidating
introDialogue:
MENU: “If your Kami isn’t enjoying Harvesting, it may not be built for such a relaxed existence.”
MENU: “Kami with a high Violence stat are more content with a life of conflict.”
MENU: “These predatory Kami can use their wild, violent natures to Liquidate other Kami in combat.”
MENU: “Unlike Harvesting, this grants a large bounty of $MUSU at one time.”
MENU: “Give it a shot if you’ve got the Kami for it. I won’t judge!”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Liquidating other Kami may be antisocial, but there’s no real harm done.”
MENU: “Just like a Kami isn’t really hurt when it’s low on Health, a Kami isn’t really dead when it’s Liquidated.”
MENU: “It may be unable to hold its body in shape for a while, but it can always come back!”
MENU: “You can revive fallen Kami with a Spell Card or some special food items."

title: Making $MUSU
introDialogue:
MENU: “Now that you’ve been harvesting for a bit, it’s time to teach you about $MUSU.”
MENU: “$MUSU is what your kami have been harvesting, it’s a form of energy that exists everywhere in the universe.”
MENU: “The Kamigotchi World has a particularly high concentration of $MUSU and $MUSU is what keeps everything here tied together, like the knots in a big rope net.”
MENU: “Collect a moderate amount of $MUSU, I’ll tell you more afterwards.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Nicely done!”
MENU: “In this world and the places that surround it, $MUSU is also a kind of currency.” 
MENU: “If you need a specific item, someone might sell just what you need, for the right price.”
MENU: “You might even get the itch to start trading goods yourself!”

title: Supporting Local Businesses
introDialogue:
MENU: “So next I’d like to have you go spend some $MUSU, just to get the hang of it.”
MENU: “The shops that should exist according to my world data are all missing, but do you remember that weird glowing door we passed earlier? It had a shop sign.”
MENU: “Why don’t you go check it out? Maybe the shop owner has some good deals.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Oof, she’s pretty ruthless, huh?”
MENU: “I guess that’s what happens when there’s no competition.”
MENU: “Oh well, maybe we’ll find a friendlier shop later.”
MENU: “And don’t worry, not everyone is trying to rip you off. Here, take this.”

objectives.description: Buy something from any vendor using $MUSU

title: Building a Reputation
introDialogue:
MENU: “This one is a more personal request.”
MENU: “I want to try and do some repairs on my systems and update my world data cache. If you can get me the raw materials, I should be able to jury-rig the parts I’ll need to do it.”
MENU: “So can you please get me a few units of Scrap Metal?”
MENU: “You should be able to find some in that anomalous junkyard beyond the torii gate.”
MENU: “I know it’s a bit inconvenient, but please? I’d really appreciate it.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Thank you! I’m feeling smarter already. Maybe now I can fix my databases and figure out what’s going on.”
MENU: “You’ve probably noticed that the quests I give you provide a variety of rewards, and that’ll be true for anyone offering you quests.”
MENU: “Sometimes they might give you items or $MUSU, but even if they don’t, you’ll always gain a little character.”
MENU: “Your operator profile uses a set of meters to track how others see you. For example, the way I see you is tracked as Reputation.”
MENU: “As your Menu, I’m what you use to interface with the Kamigotchi World.”
MENU: “Since we’re always hanging out, and I’m as friendly as it gets, raising your Reputation with me is easy.”
MENU: “I’ll always give between 2 to 6 Reputation for completing quests, but sometimes I might think you deserve more.”
MENU: “Anyone who offers you a quest will always grant you some standing with them for completing it, but they might not all be as generous about it as I am.”

rewards.description: 6x Agency Reputation,1x “Paeon’s Field of Flowers” Spell Card

title: Having a Normal One
introDialogue:
MENU: “That cache refresh definitely helped me out, the Kamigotchi World seems to have changed a lot since I was last online, but thanks to that upgrade I’m getting a feel for things again.”
MENU: “So we’re gonna take things step by step, starting with the most basic, Normal parts of the world.”
MENU: “That is to say, the Normal type room tiles.”
MENU: “Zevana should have already told you about kami and room types, but to review…
MENU: “Something with the Normal Type represents the essence of this realm in its purest form.”
MENU: “That will make them a good place to begin our investigation I think.”
MENU: “Collect three scavenges from normal type rooms and lets see what we can learn.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “These items are in fact pretty normal.”
MENU: “Something being normal is kinda like it being natural, but it’s natural for wherever it actually is, the normal thing in that place.”
MENU: “So these are very normal items for this normal place, a representative sample of normality.”
MENU: “That will be useful later, but we’ll need more information to compare it with.”

objectives.description: Make a Scavenging roll in 3 rooms of the Normal type

rewards.description: 4x Agency Reputation,1x ”Neith’s River of Life” Spell Card

title: That Eerie Feeling
introDialogue:
MENU: “The “Eerie” type comes into being when the normal state of things gets changed by something divine or supernatural.”
MENU: “If you ask me, this entire world is a little bit eerie, but there’s places where that effect is heightened enough for it to be the main influence on the local environment.”
MENU: “By comparing the items from an eerie room to ones from a normal room, we might be able to chart out how this world has been changed.”
MENU: “Collect three scavenges from eerie type rooms and let’s see what turns up.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “The results of this are rather unclear, these items seem to be no different than the ones from the normal type room.”
MENU: “Maybe that in and of itself is a bit eerie.”
MENU: “Opinions are mixed. Let’s move on.”

objectives.description: Make a Scavenging roll in 3 rooms of the Eerie type

title: Insects in the Miasma
introDialogue:
MENU: “This next part will be a little bit nasty. To be thorough with our survey, we’ll need to check out some insect type rooms.”
MENU: “The Insect type might make your skin crawl, but it’s not always about seeing bugs.”
MENU: “It’s deeper than that, it’s an energetic defilement, the kind of thing that makes you feel dirty inside and out.”
MENU: “You could think of it like a sort of corruption that the insects are drawn to.”
MENU: “Collect three scavenges from insect type rooms and I’ll compare them to our baseline.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Fascinating. It seems like items lose any energetic trace of where they came from when they’re scavenged.”
MENU: “They’re sort of platonic objects, the only metadata they carry is related to their fundamental natures.”
MENU: “While that makes the world a bit harder to study, it does mean you won’t have to worry about insect type corruption spreading into your inventory.”
MENU: “I think it’s important to take these small wins where we can get them.”

objectives.description: Make a Scavenging roll in 3 rooms of the Insect type

title: Tossed in the Scrap Heap
introDialogue:
MENU: “I’ve been putting this off, but it’s time to tackle the elephant in the room, or should I say, the scrapyard in the center of the map.”
MENU: “In my original world data, there was supposed to be a cozy little riverside town in there.”
MENU: “Instead there’s just this big pile of trash, the only thing that seems common to both world versions is the kami vending machine.”
MENU: “I shouldn’t call it trash, though, it’s more than trash, it’s scrap type rooms.”
MENU: “A Scrap Type isn’t defined as waste material that has been discarded, but as a small part of a greater whole.”
MENU: “People have the power to make tangible changes in the world.
MENU: “When they manifest will, create attachments with desire, and leave behind memories, they make a mark.”
MENU: “The remnants of those material attachments can end up as Scrap.”
MENU: “Perhaps that’s why there’s so much of it. There could have been some big world event which caused all of these remnants to accumulate here.”
MENU: “Collect three scavenges from scrap type rooms, maybe we’ll find evidence of what happened.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Somewhat unsurprisingly these results continue to be very inconclusive.”
MENU: “We’ve learned a few things, but I don’t think we’re much closer to understanding what’s going on with this world than we were before.”
MENU: “We’ll have to try some different methods of analysis.”
MENU: “Don’t worry though, I already have a plan in mind for our next steps.”

objectives.description: Make a Scavenging roll in 3 rooms of the Scrap type

rewards.description: 4x Agency Reputation,1x ”Neith’s River of Life” Spell Card

title: Identifying Materials: Wood
introDialogue:
MENU: “You probably picked up a Wooden Stick or two while out scavenging with your Kami.”
MENU: “Well, here’s a rumor: These trees are all branches of one huge tree, connected by the roots!”
MENU: “That’s why all the Wooden Sticks you’ll find are pretty much the same, no matter where you pick them up.”
MENU: “Is it true? I don’t know. I could analyze the wood’s structure in detail.”
MENU: “Collect 5 Wooden Sticks for me and I’ll look into it.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Yep. It’s wood.”
MENU: “These are in fact identical, not “pretty much” the same.”
MENU: “Exact down to the molecules. Are my sensors broken?”
MENU: “Whatever. They’re just sticks.”

title: Identifying Materials: Stone
introDialogue:
MENU: “Sometimes a rock isn’t just a rock. Sometimes it really “rocks”!”
MENU: “…”
MENU: “I’m sorry.”
MENU: “What I meant to say is: The structure of these rocks doesn’t always make geological sense.”
MENU: “It’s natural for them to be a little different. The Kamigotchi World doesn’t follow the same laws as the physical world.”
MENU: “But I want to know exactly how they differ. Collect 5 Rocks so I can run some tests.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “This is really something.”
MENU: “A couple of these rocks can’t be matched to a known type.”
MENU: “Hard to believe, but they fracture and shear like bone.”
MENU: “What kind of geological processes make a rock like that?”
MENU: “You don’t need to answer. Just thinking out loud.”

title: Identifying Materials: Metal
introDialogue:
MENU: “This is all so confusing.”
MENU: “Those upgrades we did earlier are helping but my cache is still partly corrupted and missing a bunch of data.”
MENU: “I think with a few more modifications to my systems I can build a workaround
MENU: “Get me 5 pieces of Scrap Metal, please? Just like last time.”
MENU: “And keep your fingers crossed.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “That should do the trick. Thanks a lot!”
MENU: “...”
MENU: “Well my cache seems fixed now, but there are still so many empty spaces.”
MENU: “Don’t get worried about me, but I feel like I’m missing something important.”
MENU: “Ah well. I’ll figure it out.”

title: Exploring Other Options
introDialogue:
MENU: “Well that’s two dead-ends, but I’m thinking much more clearly after that upgrade so I have some new ideas.”
MENU: “I was able to cross-check against all available world data, and from what I can tell, this world is much bigger than it seems.”
MENU: “The currently accessible zones on the map are only a small fraction of the total world area.”
MENU: “If we can find a way into those other areas we’ll probably find the answers we’re looking for.”
MENU: “So it’s time for a thorough search. I’ll collect data and look for hidden paths as you move around the map.”
MENU: “Once I know where they are, maybe I can help open them up.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Quite the workout, no? Here, this spell card will perk you up.”
MENU: “That huge lab facility stands out like a sore thumb, it’s totally out of place in this world.”
MENU: “We should definitely check it out, but it’s locked up tight for now.”
MENU: “Keep looking around, maybe there’s something we’ve missed.”

rewards.description: 2x Agency Reputation,1x ”Neith’s River of Life” Spell Card

title: Harvesting Data I
introDialogue:
MENU: “On my original maps, the area occupied by the scrapyard is supposed to be the location of the starter town, full of quest givers and shops.”
MENU: “I want to find out what happened to that town. Is there anything left from it? Did it ever exist? 
MENU: “Please hike to the deepest part of the scrapyard and check it out for me.”
MENU: “If there’s answers, they’ll be buried beneath all that scrap.”
MENU: “All that strange machinery piled up in one place…”
MENU: “It might be covering up something even more interesting.”
MENU: “Harvest for at least 12 hours in the Scrap Confluence so I can run an extended analysis.”
MENU: “If I find anything, I’ll let you know.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “I’ve completed my analysis!”
MENU: “Unfortunately I am now more confused than I was before.”
MENU: “The only things from the town that exist in this world are the torii gate, the kami vending machine, and the bell from the church steeple.”
MENU: “Nothing else from the town exists, and I’m not sure it ever existed. It’s like someone started designing it but stopped after only making the map and a few objects.”
MENU: “That’s not even the weirdest part.”
MENU: “That machine built from the church bell? It’s supposed to warp your kami through different dimensions or something crazy like that.”
MENU: “I don’t think it’s functional, but I wouldn’t advise risking your kami to test it.”
MENU: “Let’s move on.”

objectives.description: Harvest for >720 minutes in Scrap Confluence

rewards.description: 4x Agency Reputation,1x “Paeon’s Field of Flowers” Spell Card

title: Harvesting Data II
introDialogue:
MENU: “That laboratory complex on the south side of the map is an even bigger mystery than the scrapyard.”
MENU: “It’s not in any of my databases, not even the fully updated ones. It’s a complete anomaly.”
MENU: “And beyond that, there’s just something really off about the whole place. It doesn’t fit properly into the context of this world.”
MENU: “Whatever it is that’s going on here, that place seems obviously connected to it somehow.”
MENU: “We’re gonna have to find a way inside if we want answers.”
MENU: “Harvest for at least 12 hours at the Labs Entrance while I run some deep scans.”
MENU: “Maybe we’ll get lucky and find a spare key stashed under a flowerpot.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Forget about finding a key. I can’t even find the keyhole.”
MENU: “There’s some oddly specific gaps in my database around this.”
MENU: “I think someone deleted the object data for all the doors and windows to stop me from running an analysis.”
MENU: “They must have really wanted to keep us out.”
MENU: “...Whoever they are.”

objectives.description: Harvest for >720 minutes at Labs Entrance

rewards.description: 4x Agency Reputation,2x “Paeon’s Field of Flowers” Spell Card

title: Harvesting Data III
introDialogue:
MENU: “My earlier scans seem to indicate that the world map continues onwards from the temple by the waterfall.”
MENU: “Maybe there’s something behind that waterfall?”
MENU: “Go to the Hollow Path and Harvest for at least 12 hours.”
MENU: “The Temple by the Waterfall doesn’t have a Node, so that’s the closest place you can set Kami down.”
MENU: “I’ll run my tests from there and let you know if anything interesting turns up.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Good news!”
MENU: “I’ve confirmed the existence of a cave beyond the waterfall.”
MENU: “Unfortunately, I don’t think you can just jump inside.”
MENU: “I don’t mean to be rude, but you seem to abhor running water.”
MENU: “There has to be a way to get us in despite that.”
MENU: “Maybe a second entrance somewhere...”

objectives.description: Harvest for >720 minutes at the Hollow Path

rewards.description: 4x Agency Reputation,1x “Paeon’s Field of Flowers” Spell Card,1x ”Melkarth’s Heroic Awakening” Spell Card

title: Squaring the Circle I
introDialogue:
MENU: “The holes in my memory are frustrating.”
MENU: “I should know how to progress, but it’s like someone wanted me to forget.”
MENU: “Bear with me for a while, okay? I have one more thing to try.”
MENU: “A long, thorough, final search around the map, clockwise from the top.”
MENU: “We’ll find something.”
MENU: “Start at Scrap Trees and dig around. I’ll connect to your Kami and share what they learn.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “I thought we’d find something juicy in that notebook, but the writing is just weird poetry.”
MENU: “Not much of it either. It’s more of a sketchbook, really.”
MENU: “Most of the drawings are pictures of the same young woman.”
MENU: “She looks kind of familiar, but I can’t place her.”
MENU: “The rest of them look like monsters…” 
MENU: “Some of them are kind of scary, but others look cute. They kind of resemble the Kamigotchi.”
MENU: “The word “Moon” was written on the inside cover. Does that mean something to you?”

objectives.description: Make 2 Scavenging rolls at Scrap Trees

title: Squaring the Circle II
introDialogue:
MENU: “Continue moving clockwise around the map.”
MENU: “Next up, visit Centipedes and send your Kami out to scavenge.”
MENU: “Is there something in that hole? It seems dangerous there.”
MENU: “The insects really thrive in that part of the woods. More than most places.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “It’s disgusting.”
MENU: “Something under there is exceedingly rotten.”
MENU: “It’s so far gone that I can’t tell what it was originally. Just a carpet of worms now.”
MENU: “I would have preferred to find some hidden treasure.”
MENU: “Nothing else to do here for now.”

title: Squaring the Circle III
introDialogue:
MENU: “We haven’t gotten answers yet, but we’ve made a little progress. 
MENU: “More information helps. More context helps.”
MENU: “Even if we don’t find something with a direct connection to the labs, I feel like we’re on the right track.”
MENU: “Next, visit the Blooming Tree and make scavenging rolls.”
MENU: “The weather here is always clear. It wasn’t lightning, so what blasted that tree apart?
MENU: “It probably won’t open any doors for us, but I’m still curious.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Didn’t come up with anything useful. That tree is still a mystery.”
MENU: “It’s got a certain presence, that’s for sure.”
MENU: “I thought it was dead, but it’s still hanging on.”
MENU: “It’s probably one of the oldest things in this place. My circuits might corrode before it grows back, though.”
MENU: “Interesting, but not what we’re looking for. Let’s keep going.”

objectives.description: Make 3 Scavenging Rolls at Blooming Tree

title: Squaring the Circle IV
introDialogue:
MENU: “Visit the Airplane Crash and scavenge around with your Kami.”
MENU: “I haven’t mentioned that plane until now, but that’s because I have no clue where it came from or what it’s doing here.
MENU: “I’m supposed to have pretty thorough data for this area!”
MENU: “It’s not a gap I feel an absence from like the starter town or the labs data, this thing is a genuine foreign body.”
MENU: “What’s the story? Who was on it? Where did they go? Could we follow them?”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “A small private jet with one pilot and four passengers. 
MENU: “They drew a primitive representation of their party on the interior roof of the plane.”
MENU: “Later, something drove them away from this place. The last thing they left was this journal.”
MENU: “If we find any of these people hanging around, you might want to talk to them.”
MENU: “Still, I don’t think pursuing this story will help us pass the waterfall. We should move on.”

objectives.description: Make 3 Scavenging Rolls at Airplane Crash

title: Squaring the Circle V
introDialogue:
MENU: “Visit the Clearing and do a little scavenging. Do your best to not disturb the cairn.”
MENU: “Mounds of stone like this are often meant as burial mounds.
MENU: “So who or what is buried here?”
MENU: “With every dead end we lose another lead and pile on more junk data.”
MENU: “Let’s hope this one has something useful.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “That’s strange. There’s absolutely nothing here.”
MENU: “I don’t feel good about this search as a whole. We’re turning up so much information, but it’s all irrelevant.”
MENU: “I apologize for being so cold regarding the passengers of that private jet.”
MENU: “I’m just focused on something else.”
MENU: “It’s time to get moving.”

title: Squaring the Circle VI
introDialogue:
MENU: “Let’s keep working our way around the perimeter of the map. Go back to the Labs Entrance one more time and make scavenging rolls.”
MENU: “Where did that building come from and why is it sealed up so well? Who sealed it up like that?”
MENU: “It honestly really bothers me. When we get the doors open, I’m going to have so many questions.”
resolutionDialogue:
MENU: “Someone’s definitely inside, and they definitely locked us out on purpose.”
MENU: “I don’t know why they’d do that, though.”
MENU: “Aren’t you supposed to go this way?“
MENU: “I managed to get a list of users that passed through these doors. I’m still making the connections, but one of them…

introDialogue:

MINA: “Memorable dreams or intense nightmares, powerful emotions, or even raw physical sensations such as touch, sight, or sound.”
MINA: “That stuff can make for a really powerful reagent.”
MINA: “There’s a swirl in the currents like that in this room, and so this is a good place to scavenge some.”
MINA: “What are you waiting for? You won’t learn magic if you just keep standing there.”
